title: fix(sse): correct chunking/framing for partial JSON tokens and delimiter ordering
author: Ava Thompson
ci_status: fail (one flaky unit test) -> pass (after rerun)
body: Context: We observed production errors where SSE clients consuming partial JSON payloads would occasionally receive malformed events when tokens were split across chunk boundaries or when delimiter events ("[DELIM]" markers used internally) interleaved with token events in non-deterministic order. This caused downstream JSON parsing failures and client-side partial JSON state corruption. Motivation: Stabilize streaming output so consumers (including the OpenAI compatibility layer and SDKs) can rely on deterministic token/event ordering and well-formed partial JSON segments. Changes: 1) Framer: ensure that token boundaries are emitted with atomic framing decisions so partial JSON tokens are never delivered with an intermediate delimiter event. When a token spans chunks we now buffer until the token end is known or a configured max-chunk delay is reached. 2) Delimiters: change internal delimiter insertion so delimiters are always emitted after token events for the same logical output and never inserted mid-token. This prevents parsers from seeing delimiter events before completing token content. 3) Token/event ordering: added explicit sequencing metadata (internal only) to guarantee ordered delivery under concurrent batch flushes; removed an unsafe parallel flush path in the Rust framer that could reorder events under high concurrency. 4) OpenAI compat: small adjustments to the compat layer to preserve event ordering for legacy consumers and to interpret the updated delimiter semantics. 5) Tests and docs: new regression tests covering partial JSON reconstruction, token-splitting across chunk boundaries, and simulated network chunk reordering. Updated docs/streaming.md to outline guarantees and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure with unit/regression test - [x] Implement fixes in framer and compat layer - [x] Add tests for token-splitting and delimiter ordering - [x] Add integration test against compatibility shim - [x] Update docs and changelog - [x] CI green (after rerun)

t6u7v8w: docs: streaming guarantees and migration notes
review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice catch on the delimiter ordering - can you add an explicit unit test that simulates a token split across two chunks and ensures the delimiter arrives afterwards?
Ava Thompson: Added test test_partial_json_token_split() and an integration that replays reordered chunk delivery to the framer. The test also asserts no mid-token delimiter insertion.
Priya Singh: The Rust change removes the parallel flush path; any perf impact? Can we add a micro-benchmark?

Ava Thompson: Added sse_chunking_bench.py and ran locally; there's a <2% regression under synthetic worst-case but the deterministic ordering fixes production correctness issues. We can consider later optimizations (batch coalescing) to regain perf.
Ethan Zhang: CI failed on one flaky test in test_streaming_adapter; reran and all checks passed. Approving after CI green.
Priya Singh: Approve after adding a note in streaming.md about the delimiter semantics change for consumers that relied on previous ordering (rare).
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming: ensure partial JSON tokens are emitted atomically and delimiter events maintain ordering to avoid consumer-side JSON parsing errors. Includes regression tests and doc updates.
